messages:
Lena Ortiz: Quick heads-up - the new JS SDK sample uploaded to Cloudflare Workers errors out during cold start: `ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined` and then `Uncaught ReferenceError: require is not defined`. Anyone on edge compat duty?
Marcelo Ruiz: yup that's the classic Node -> Worker leak. Which sample? the one that uses `form-data` or `node-fetch`?
Lena Ortiz: it's the small chat sample that sends an image as base64. We used `Buffer.from` to decode and a tiny helper that `require('node-fetch')` in the helper. Works in Node, fails in Wrangler.
Priya Singh: Workers is pure web runtime. No Buffer, no process, no require. For base64 use web APIs: `const bytes = Uint8Array.from(atob(s), c => c.charCodeAt(0))` and `btoa` to encode. Replace node-fetch with the platform `fetch`.
Sophia Chen: we should stop shipping a single universal bundle. Maintain two outputs: `dist/edge.mjs` (browser platform, no Node shims) and `dist/node.cjs` (node platform). Then set package.json exports so `import` users on edge can point at edge.mjs.
Marcelo Ruiz: agreed. Also add an `isEdge()` runtime detection: `const IS_EDGE = typeof process === 'undefined' && typeof WebSocket !== 'undefined'` so samples can pick lightweight implementations.
Lena Ortiz: what about auth refresher? our SDK uses `setInterval` to refresh tokens periodically. That won't run reliably on Workers.
Priya Singh: edge functions are short-lived. Use on-demand refresh: check expiry at request time and refresh synchronously if needed. Or use signed short-lived tokens rather than long-lived server timers. Document this pattern in the sample.
Sophia Chen: typings note: TS users targeting Node often don't include `DOM` libs so `fetch` types vanish. In sample tsconfig recommend "lib": ["ES2021","DOM"] or add `/// <reference lib="dom" />` at top of example file.
Marcelo Ruiz: more gotchas: some transitive deps reference `process.env.NODE_ENV`. If bundler doesn't replace that, you'll get `process is not defined` at runtime. For the edge build use esbuild define: { 'process.env.NODE_ENV': '"production"' } and platform: 'browser'.
Lena Ortiz: should we add a tiny `edge-shim.ts` in samples that exports `encodeBase64`, `decodeBase64`, `randomUUID`, and `isEdge`? That keeps the sample tiny and explicit.
Sophia Chen: yes. Use `crypto.randomUUID()` where available and fallback to `crypto.getRandomValues`+encoding when not. Provide small typed helpers so consumers don't have to think about WebCrypto vs NodeCrypto.
Marcelo Ruiz: CI suggestion: add a smoke test job that runs samples against Miniflare or Wrangler dev in CI. Fast check to catch `process`/`Buffer` leaks before releases.
Priya Singh: also check bundles for accidental polyfills. Avoid bringing `buffer` or `stream` shims into edge build; size matters.
Lena Ortiz: I'll open a PR to: (1) convert the sample to use `edge.mjs` entry, (2) remove node-fetch and Buffer refs, (3) add edge-shim.ts in samples, and (4) add a miniflare smoke test.
Devex-Bot: Noted: internal doc updated https://redwood-internal.example.com/devex/edge/sdk-compat with Marcelo's build flags and Sophia's TS tips.
Lena Ortiz: PR coming in a few hours. Thanks all :sparkles:
